title: Lim Seng at your door
body:
After the evening prayer, Lim Seng of Guangzhou waits outside your house with a lacquered box of tea. He has traded here for years, he says, and never knew his factor carried another man’s jars. Tan Bo is held for the temenggung’s judgement; the fish-marked nutmeg belongs to a merchant the court has suspended.

Lim Seng asks one thing: that you tell the temenggung the porcelain and silk were honestly his, so his name is not struck with his factor’s.

choices.label: Speak for Lim Seng’s good name
choices.outcome_text: You send a note to the temenggung’s house: the cleared cargo was Lim Seng’s, the after-row jars were not. Lim Seng bows low. Before he leaves he says the boatman who rowed the fish-marked jars out to the Kim Hong works for a Javanese broker in Upeh.

choices.label: Return the tea and say nothing
choices.outcome_text: You hand back the box unopened. A shahbandar who takes gifts on the night of a ruling is a shahbandar whose rulings can be bought. Lim Seng leaves stiffly; the Chinese captains at anchor will hear that you could not be moved.

choices.label: Accept the tea, promise nothing
choices.outcome_text: You take the box and promise to consider it. By the morning tide half the waterfront says the shahbandar was paid after the Kim Hong ruling, and nobody is sure for what.
